title: Token trajectory cost carousel — compact per-invocation attribution and export prototype
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Design a compact, horizontally scrollable 'trajectory carousel' for the Redwood Console that surfaces token-level cost breakdowns and attribution per-invocation without overwhelming observers.
description_details: Scope: single-console panel that can be embedded in Route and Model dashboards. Focus on per-invocation forensic view (first-party metadata, prompt vs completion token split, KV-cache reuse indicator, batch attribution), timeline sparklines, and a lightweight CSV/JSON export. Constraints: must work in dense dashboard rows, degrade to summary rows on small screens, and respect PII/data tenancy rules for Private deployments.
design_goals: 1) Fast scan: enable engs/product owners to identify expensive invocations within 3 taps. 2) Attribution clarity: clearly show which tokens were charged, cached, or re-requested. 3) Exportable: allow export of visible tokens and derived attributions with trace IDs. 4) Minimal cognitive load: avoid deep modal plumbing for quick investigations.
comments: 2026-03-02 — PM review (Ravi Shah): Likes carousel for temporal browsing; requested a compact mode for routes table integration.
2026-03-04 — Eng feedback (Maya Li): Backend will provide token-level deltas and a cache-hit boolean; asked design to avoid showing raw tokens, only token counts and fingerprints for privacy.
2026-03-06 — Design decision: replace raw token preview with hashed token fingerprint + human-friendly label ("prompt-prefix", "completion-final") to meet privacy constraints.
2026-03-07 — Prototype uploaded and shared for review. Notes from usability test (3 engineers): carousel is discoverable but horizontal scroll needs keyboard affordance and focus outline.
2026-03-09 — Accessibility review (Hannah Cole): Ensure contrast for mini-sparkline and that export button has aria-label and is reachable via keyboard shortcuts.
2026-03-10 — PM sign-off pending two small changes: 1) CSV header order must match API contract, 2) add 'attribution confidence' tag when model fallback used.
Follow-ups planned: add a canary metric to Console demonstrating feature usage and conversion to rerun/reprofile flow.
acceptance_criteria: Visual prototype (Figma) shows carousel in both dense row embedding and full-panel modes
Prototype includes: invocation row, token-split badges (prompt/completion/cache), mini-sparkline of cost over token offset, fingerprint label and 'view details' affordance
Export action produces CSV/JSON matching spec and respects tenancy (no raw token content for Private customers)
Accessibility: keyboard navigation, aria-labels for export and key controls, color contrast verified
Performance: UI renders first 10 invocations < 150ms in console staging with typical route payloads
ux_notes: Carousel items are grouped by 1-minute buckets by default with zoom to invocation timeline
Hover state surfaces a micro-timeline tooltip with cost delta and KV-cache reuse percent
Compact mode collapses sparkline to a single colored bar and shows aggregate token count
Export button exposes 'visible range' and 'full-run' options; default is visible range
When fallback to cheaper model occurs, attribution confidence shows as Low/Medium/High
